architecture.mechanism: CFD-based design optimization using 3D airflow analysis to identify and implement aerodynamic shape modifications that reduce drag.
architecture.intervention: Apply CFD-based design optimization to the passenger vehicle body, focusing on frontal area, roofline, underbody, and rear geometry, to develop drag-reducing features such as optimized front fascia, active grille shutters, underbody panels, and rear diffuser/spoiler, validated through scaled wind tunnel testing.
architecture.expected_effect: Significant reduction in aerodynamic drag coefficient (Cd) leading to lower total energy consumption at highway speeds while maintaining interior space, safety, and manufacturability at mainstream cost.
architecture.falsification_test: Conduct CFD simulation of baseline passenger vehicle and optimized design at highway speeds (e.g., 100 km/h); if drag reduction is less than 10% or if interior space/safety/manufacturability constraints are violated, the mechanism fails.
